analysis:
The PR changes documentation only. docs/operations/provider-release.md adds a sentence at head lines ~632-636, and docs/provider/cli-reference.md adds a paragraph at ~1577-1588 plus a date bump. The additions describe a release-lane check, scripts/check-provider-weak-imports.py, which refuses binaries importing Foundation's back-deployed Date.>= and Date.<=. They also describe scripts/check-date-comparisons.py, which refuses the same pattern in source. Both exist to avoid crashes on pre-release macOS 27.2 builds. No code, workflow, entitlement, signing, attestation, key-handling or coordinator contract change is visible in the supplied evidence. The release flow itself is unchanged: signing, notarization, staging, registration and the hash-pinned payload. The rest of provider-release.md (lines 455-1130) was supplied as head text and is unmodified context. That context describes existing release controls and cluster_runtime handling, and I found no regression there.

The new text strengthens an availability control, since it prevents a provider crash loop (relevant to T-057). It does not weaken any trust boundary (TB-009, TB-011) or asset (A-011, A-017).

The new check scripts and their CI wiring are not in the supplied batch. I cannot verify that they work or are enforced, but doc claims alone do not create a security regression. A later pass that sees the scripts or workflow changes should confirm they fail closed and do not alter the signing or secret-handling steps. The cluster-runtime and dev-branch release lane prose appears unchanged by this PR.
